statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 5% (low), Stress 38% (moderate), Confidence 87% (high). Venue halted for the entire published horizon.
recommendation: Tail sits at a closed-market floor and the mapped policy state is EA_ON. No danger window is published, because no venue quotes at any point in this horizon and there is therefore no evidence-based interval to flag. The material forward checkpoint falls outside the window: the Sunday 22:00 UTC futures reopen, where accumulated weekend developments in the US-Iran conflict and any further shift in September Fed pricing would be expressed as a single gap rather than as an observable price path. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by the mapped state, and subsequent assessment cycles will score the reopen once a live path exists.
headline: Nasdaq-100 closed the payroll week at 29,544.15 after an orderly two-way session; with futures settled since 21:00 UTC the full 24-hour horizon is a halted venue and Tail rests at a closed-market floor
body: The Nasdaq-100 ended Friday's August payroll session at 29,544.15, up 0.21% from a 29,482.32 prior close, having opened at 29,539.57, extended to 29,655.22, fully retraced that advance to a 29,440.15 low and recovered into the cash close. Retracement occurred repeatedly in both directions, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. CME equity index futures then settled at 21:00 UTC, so there is no live price path for NQ futures or the NAS100 CFD at this assessment and none will exist until the Sunday 22:00 UTC reopen, roughly twenty five hours after the final published hour. Monday 7 September is the US Labor Day holiday. The index outperformed a weaker tape: the S&P 500 fell 0.38% to 7,718.41, the Dow lost 0.51% to 53,413.60 and the Nasdaq Composite eased 0.29% to 26,506.99, with semiconductors up about 3.4% on the session against a 2.1% decline in software and services. That dispersion is a rotation signature rather than the aligned single-direction stack that would justify a raised Tail. Volatility confirmed the orderly reading, with VIX closing at 14.53, up 1.47%, inside a 13.80-14.58 range. The August employment report, verified at the BLS release, printed 162,000 nonfarm payrolls against roughly 53,000 to 56,000 expected, with 55,000 of upward revisions to prior months, unemployment steady at 4.1% and average hourly earnings up 0.3% on the month to $37.75 and 3.1% over the year. Rate transmission stayed contained rather than disorderly: the 10-year yield rose about 2.2 basis points to 4.784% while the 2-year traded near 4.42%, its highest since January 2025, and September hike pricing firmed to roughly 58% from about 49% a day earlier ahead of the 15-16 September FOMC. The H.15 release still shows 3 September as its latest official column, at 4.34% and 4.77%. Energy remains the live geopolitical channel: WTI settled at $91.48, up 0.20%, and Brent at $92.68, up 0.8%, for weekly gains near 10% and 7.6% as US-Iran hostilities resumed, with four Hormuz transits on Thursday against a ten-day average near fifteen and US diesel at a record $5.85 per gallon. Delayed shared cross-asset context, used only as supporting evidence, showed the same dispersion rather than one-way index structure, with latest-session NQ marginally positive against weaker ES and YM and semiconductor industry groups strongly higher. With the venue halted for the entire horizon, Tail is published at a closed-market floor of 5%, while Stress at 38% represents unpriced weekend exposure to active Middle East escalation and a firmer September rate path rather than any observed drawdown.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours span the calm pre-payroll regime, the August employment release, its decay into the Friday cash close and the start of the weekend halt. Tail sat at 12-13% through the Asian hours and drifted to 17% into the European session while Stress climbed steadily from 51% to 62% ahead of the print. The 12:00 UTC hour carried the only genuine spike, with Tail at 24%, Stress at 76% and Confidence down to 74% as event/whipsaw conditions took over on the 162,000 payroll surprise. Price discovery then proved orderly: the initial move was retraced, Tail fell to 20% and 18% over the following two hours and back into the low teens through the US afternoon, with dominant mode moving from event/whipsaw to mixed as semiconductor strength offset megacap weakness. The final hour steps down to a 5% closed-market floor with Stress at 38% as futures settled. The published series remained EA_ON and green for 22 of the 24 hours, with WATCH and yellow only in the two hours immediately around the release.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the weekend halt. CME equity index futures settled at 21:00 UTC on Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday 6 September, roughly twenty five hours after this horizon ends, and Monday 7 September is the US Labor Day holiday. Because no venue quotes during any published hour, the pathological price path that Tail measures cannot form, so forecast Tail is held at a 4-5% closed-market floor and the dominant mode of normal denotes a halted rather than a directional regime. Stress starts at 38% and drifts to 42% through Saturday to reflect weekend information accumulating unpriced against active US-Iran hostilities and a firmer September rate path; that exposure is real for anything carried through the break but is expressed as a single reopen gap rather than as a tradable path. Confidence decays from 87% to 78% purely with distance from the verified Friday evidence cutoff, since coverage itself is complete. No macro release falls inside the horizon; the next verified checkpoints are PPI on 10 September and CPI on 11 September, both at 12:30 UTC, ahead of the 15-16 September FOMC.
